fn.sin: sine (angle in radians — rad(30) converts degrees)
fn.asin: arc sine — result in radians (deg(...) converts to degrees)
fn.atan2: atan2(y, x) — angle of the vector (x, y) in radians
fn.floor: round down to a whole number
fn.ceil: round up to a whole number
fn.clamp: clamp(x, from, to) — x limited to the interval
fn.lerp: lerp(a, b, t) — from a to b: t = 0 gives a, t = 1 gives b
fn.exp: e to the power of x
fn.hypot: hypot(x, y) — length of the vector
fn.mod: mod(a, b) — remainder, always from 0 to b (also for negative numbers)
fn.step: step(edge, x) — 0 before the edge, 1 from the edge on
fn.smooth: smooth(from, to, x) — smoothly from 0 to 1 as x goes from “from” to “to”
fn.rand: rand(x) — a “random” number 0–1, always the same for the same x (e.g. rand(i) for each copy)
fn.onstep: onstep(x, step) — 1 when x lies on the step grid (onstep(2.25, 0.25) → 1): a condition for random tasks so that the solution can be set
fn.root: root(x, n) — n-th root (root(27, 3) → 3; of a negative number only for odd n)
fn.log: log(x) — base 10, log(x, b) — base b: log(8, 2) → 3
fn.sig: sig(x, n) — rounding to n significant digits: sig(0.012345, 2) → 0.012
fn.fact: fact(n) — factorial n! (n a whole number 0–170)
fn.binom: binom(n, k) — binomial coefficient: how many ways to choose k out of n
fn.isint: isint(x) — 1 when x is a whole number (condition: the result must be whole)
fn.fmt: fmt(x, digits) — number as text with a decimal comma: fmt(9.81, 1) → "9,8"
fn.fmtpi: fmtpi(x, digits) — number as a multiple of π: fmtpi(2.356) → "0,75π", fmtpi(3.1416) → "π" (up to 2 places, no trailing zeros)

listFn.len: len(x) — how many items a list has (or characters a text)
listFn.at: at(list, i) — the item at place i, counting from 0 (−1: the last); same as list[i]
listFn.take: take(list, k) — the first k items
listFn.drop: drop(list, k) — without the first k items
listFn.slice: slice(list, from, to) — a piece: from inclusive, to exclusive (from 0; negative counts from the end)
listFn.sort: sort(list) — ascending: numbers by value, texts alphabetically, entries by name (descending: reverse(sort(list)))
listFn.shuffle: shuffle(list) — randomly shuffled (the task’s draw: same task number, same order)
listFn.choose: choose(list, k) — k different items chosen at random (no repeats)
listFn.pick: pick(list) — one item chosen at random
listFn.contains: contains(list, x) — 1 when x is in the list (for a text: when the text contains x)
listFn.index: index(list, x) — the place of x in the list, from 0 (−1: not there)
listFn.range: range(from, to, step) — numbers from…to INCLUSIVE (range(1, 5) → [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]); step defaults to 1
listFn.join: join(list, separator) — the items in one text (comma by default)
listFn.concat: concat(a, b, …) — lists joined into one (a single value is added as an item)
listFn.list: list(a, b, …) — a list of these values (same as [a, b, …])
listFn.get: get(entry, "key") — a field of the entry by key (same as entry.key)
listFn.str: str(x) — as text; a number with a decimal comma, up to 12 significant digits
listFn.num: num(text) — a number from a text ("3,5" → 3.5)
listFn.sub: sub(x) — digits and the signs + − ( ) as subscript: "SO" + sub(4) → "SO₄"
listFn.plain: plain(x) — sub- and superscripts back to plain characters: "Al₂(SO₄)₃" → "Al2(SO4)3"
listFn.gcd: gcd(a, b, …) — greatest common divisor of whole numbers (lists too)
listFn.lcm: lcm(a, b, …) — least common multiple (lists too): lcm(3, 2) → 6

lazyFn.if: if(condition, a, b) — a when the condition holds, otherwise b (same as condition ? a : b)
lazyFn.filter: filter(list, condition) — the items for which the condition holds: filter(jony, it.ladunek > 0)
lazyFn.map: map(list, expression) — the expression for each item: map(wydarzenia, it.label)
lazyFn.sortby: sortby(list, key) — ascending by the expression: sortby(wydarzenia, it.data) — earliest first
lazyFn.find: find(list, condition) — the first item that meets the condition (none: "")
lazyFn.any: any(list, condition) — 1 when at least one item meets the condition
lazyFn.all: all(list, condition) — 1 when every item meets the condition
lazyFn.count: count(list) — how many items; count(list, condition) — how many meet the condition
lazyFn.sum: sum(list) or sum(list, expression) — the sum: sum(skladniki, it.masa)
lazyFn.avg: avg(list) or avg(list, expression) — the average
lazyFn.min: min(a, b, …) — the smallest number; min(list); min(list, expression)
lazyFn.max: max(a, b, …) — the largest number; max(list); max(list, expression)
lazyFn.minby: minby(list, key) — the item with the smallest key: minby(wydarzenia, it.data) — the earliest
lazyFn.maxby: maxby(list, key) — the item with the largest key

expr.unclosedText: unclosed text — a quotation mark is missing
expr.tooDeep: the expression is nested too deeply
expr.fieldAfterDot: a field name was expected after the dot
expr.breaksOff: the expression breaks off — something is missing
expr.needsEach: {fn}({set}, …) needs an expression after the comma
expr.listTooLong: a list in the expression has more than {n} items
expr.needsParens: “{name}” is a function — it needs parentheses: {name}(…)
expr.dotOnlyInWorld: “{path}” — a dot in a name only works in a world (“world”)
expr.afterDot: “{path}” — after the dot: parent, root, outer or self

exprHelp.intro: Expressions (values computed on the fly) — text, e.g. "v0*cos(rad(kat))":
exprHelp.numbers: numbers: 3, 0.5, 2e-3 (decimal point); texts in apostrophes: 'ok'; names: variables, computed values, simulation state and built-in names
exprHelp.compare: comparisons: < <= > >= == != — give 1 (yes) or 0 (no); logic: && (and), || (or), ! (not); condition: w ? a : b
exprHelp.text: text + number joins text (number with a decimal comma, up to 3 places); fmt(x, digits) — number with a chosen number of places
exprHelp.constants: constants: pi, tau (2·pi), e, true (1), false (0) — an own variable with such a name (e.g. "e" as the coefficient of restitution) takes precedence
exprHelp.angles: Angles: sin/cos/tan work in radians — rad(angle) converts an angle in degrees, deg(...) converts the result of asin/acos/atan2.
exprHelp.world: In a world ("world"): parent.x, root.x — value of the parent, of the root (parent.parent.x — of the grandparent); outer.x — of the thing that is summing up; name.x — of the thing with that "id"
exprHelp.can: can — 1 when the person may change something in this thing (drag, set), 0 when it is given; can.pos — when they may change "pos" in particular (e.g. colour for given vs changeable, arrows ↔)
exprHelp.end: An unknown name is an error (the editor shows where); division by 0 gives infinity — such a shape is not drawn for the moment.
exprHelp.aggregates: summaries: {list} — e.g. sum(children, total*arm), count(children), count(odwaznik, mass > 5), all(belka, abs(mom) < 0.05)
exprHelp.sets: sets: children, descendants (all below), siblings, others (others of this kind), things (all) or the name of a kind; the expression after the comma is computed in EACH thing of the set (its names, its parent), and outer.x reaches the one that asks
exprHelp.lists: lists (e.g. range(1, 10)): {list} — described in Cogita’s generated tasks; in filter/map/sortby… "it" is the item, "i" its place

genHelp.intro: Expressions in generated tasks — the same language as in drawings (numbers with a decimal point, texts in apostrophes, + - * / % ^, < <= > >= == !=, && || !, w ? a : b), plus:
genHelp.lists: lists: [1, 2, 3], [a, b]; item: list[0] (from 0; list[-1] — the last); list + list — joined
genHelp.entry: entry (drawn from the base): entry.field (e.g. kation.ladunek), entry.id, entry.label; a number field with a quantity: entry.field_si (in SI), entry.field_unit; date: entry.date (number yyyymmdd, for comparisons), entry.date_text (in words); reference: entry.period.label (one step further)
genHelp.each: an expression for each item (filter, map, sortby, count, any, all, find, sum, avg, min, max, minby, maxby): "it" — the item, "i" — its place (from 0), e.g. filter(jony, it.ladunek < 0), map(wydarzenia, it.label)
genHelp.compare: texts compare alphabetically ("Ala" < "Ola"); == also compares lists (item by item) and entries (by id)
genHelp.random: drawing at random in an expression (shuffle, choose, pick) uses the task number — the same number gives the same task
genHelp.listFns: functions for lists, texts and entries:
genHelp.limits: Limits: a list up to {items} items, up to {work} steps over lists in one expression — more gives NaN (the task is not drawn).

move.label: Moves
move.says: changes place: "to": [x, y] — to a point (from "from", usually [0, 0]), or "path": [[x, y], …] — along a way through the points ("times": when at each, 0–1)

size.label: Changes size
size.says: grows or shrinks: "from" → "to" (1 — as it is; a number or [width, height])

turn.label: Turns
turn.says: turns: "from" → "to" in degrees (360 — a full turn)

reveal.label: Reveals
reveal.says: is revealed from the left: "from" → "to" (0 — nothing, 1 — all of it)

keys.label: Frames
keys.says: everything at once, frame by frame: "keys": [{ "at": 0–1, "x", "y", "scale", "sx", "sy", "rotate", "opacity", "blur", "draw", "color", "stroke", "glow", "reveal", "clip", "ease" }]

draw.label: Draws itself
draw.says: a line is drawn from start to end: "from" → "to" (0 — nothing, 1 — all of it; below 0 — nothing for a moment longer, above 1 (up to 10) — finished before the motion ends)

rise.label: Rises
rise.says: appears, rising a few pixels — slide text after arriving

assemble.label: Assembles
assemble.says: a layer appears, slightly raised and scaled down; the next ones, with growing delay, assemble the sign

focus.label: Comes into focus
focus.says: from a slight blur and from below into focus

float.label: Floats
float.says: sways gently by a few pixels and comes back

breathe.label: Breathes
breathe.says: grows and brightens, shrinks and fades

drift.label: Drifts
drift.says: moves slowly diagonally and grows, then returns — background, mist

sway.label: Sways
sway.says: waves up and down very slowly, stretching vertically — background threads

wave.label: Wave
wave.says: flows sideways and vertically along an irregular way — bands of waves

blink.label: Blinks
blink.says: dims and flares up — a warning, an error

desc.intro: Motion ("motion") — on a module on a slide and in a presentation scene, on a layer of a layered picture, on a background layer and on every element of a drawing ("animation"):
desc.shape: { "name": "move", "to": [40, -12], "duration": 900, "delay": 120, "repeat": "once", "ease": "inOut" } or a list of up to three of them (outermost first); the plain word "rise" is enough too
desc.times: "duration", "delay" — in milliseconds; for a looping motion "delay" may be negative (it starts mid-cycle)
desc.repeat: "repeat" — "once" (once, when the thing is reached; again on the next arrival — until then it stays at the first frame), "loop" (over and over while visible), "alternate" (there and back), or a number of repeats
desc.ease: "ease" — how it passes from frame to frame: "linear", "ease", "in", "out", "inOut", "step" or "cubic-bezier(a, b, c, d)"
desc.unit: "unit" — "px" (usually; in a drawing — drawing units) or "%" (percent of its own size)
desc.by: "by" — only in a presentation scene: the motion follows not the clock but the PROGRESS of the scene — "scene" (inside the scene: from the first to the last step), "enter" (the scene coming in), "leave" (the scene going out); 0 — the first frame, 1 — the last. Scrolling back reverses the motion, stopping stops it; "duration", "delay" and "repeat" then play no role
desc.verbs: Basic words (any motion can be built from them):
desc.frame: Frame ("keys"): "at" 0–1 — when; "x", "y" — shift; "scale" or "sx", "sy" — size; "rotate" — degrees; "opacity" 0–1; "blur" — blur in px;
desc.frame2: "draw" — how much of the line is drawn (0–1); "color" — fill or text colour; "stroke" — line colour; "glow" — a glow "x y blur colour" (e.g. "0 0 10px rgba(160, 220, 255, 0.75)");
desc.frame3: "reveal" 0–1 — how much is visible from the left; "clip" — a cut-out "inset(top right bottom left round 1rem)", a circle "circle(40% at 50% 50%)" or an oval "ellipse(60% 40% at 50% 50%)" (with "by" — a mask that grows with progress); "ease" — the passage to the next frame. What a frame does not give flows in one motion between the frames that give it; before the first such frame — as the thing is by itself, after the last — it stays.
desc.colors: Colours: "#rrggbb", "rgba(…)", theme names "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted", "ok", "danger" — with "/35" at the end: 35 % opacity.
desc.presets: Ready-made motions (from the old Cogita show) — entrances:
desc.reduced: With the system setting “reduce motion” nothing moves — everything stands as described without motion.

live.intro: A drawing to move ("animation" with the keys below) — a person sets something (slider, drag, button) and sees the effect at once; there may also be a simulation (motion from equations) and a goal to reach. Just like Brilliant lessons: first doing, then explaining.
live.vars: "vars" — values to set (up to {n}): [{ "name": "kat", "value": 45, "min": 0, "max": 90, "step": 1, "unit": "°", "label": "Angle", "random": [from, to] }] — "random": a different value from the interval each time it opens (in Cogita: on each attempt)
live.let: "let" — values computed from others, in this order, anew in every frame: [{ "name": "zasieg", "value": "v0^2*sin(rad(2*kat))/g" }]
live.events: "events": [{ "when": "y < 0 && vy < 0", "set": { "y": "-y", "vy": "-e*vy" }, "stop": false, "say": "Bounce!", "mood": "info" }] — when the condition BECOMES true (collision, bounce, end); "set" computes all values at once and only then assigns them,
live.until: "until": "t > 5" (end), "dt": 0.002 (step in s), "speed": 1 (pace), "auto": true (starts by itself when the drawing is visible; otherwise the "run" button), "loop": true (again after the end), "max": 600 (longest, s), "sleep": true (falls asleep when nothing moves any more and wakes on a change) }
live.rk4: Computed with the 4th-order Runge-Kutta method in fixed steps — on a slow phone the result is the same. Changing a value the start depends on restarts the simulation; changing a value in "rate" (e.g. gravity) takes effect at once.
live.slider: { "type": "slider", "var": "kat", "label": "Angle", "unit": "°", "digits": 0 } — a slider (range and step from "vars"); "number" — a number field;
live.rules: "rules" — rules (up to {n}): [{ "when": "abs(x - cel) < 0.5 && y <= 0", "say": "Hit at {fmt(kat,0)}°!", "mood": "ok"|"miss"|"info", "goal": true, "once": true, "set": {…}, "do": "pause", "go": "next" }]
live.rules2: acts when the condition BECOMES true (checked after every simulation step — flying through a hoop counts too); "say" appears below the drawing ({…} — computed);
live.goal: "goal": true — this is the goal: reached = task solved (in Cogita: a correct answer); "go" — in a presentation: "next" (onward), "back", a scene key or "link:<id>"; "for": 1 — the condition must hold this many seconds without a break (“steadily”)
live.show: every control may have "show": "solved" — it is visible only when the expression is true (e.g. a “Next” button after solving)
live.predict: "predict" — predict first, then see: true or { "start": true, "say": "…", "check": "Check", "again": "Adjust", "hold": "Predict" }; the drawing stands still (simulation stopped, rules silent, no goal) while the person sets their prediction; “Check” lets it run, “Adjust” (or any change after checking) stops it again; "start": false — runs at once, and “Predict” stops it on request.
live.held: In expressions "held" = 1 while it stands still — whatever gives away the result waits: "stroke": "=held ? 'ink' : (ok ? 'ok' : 'danger')", "show": "!held"; "tries" — how many times it has been checked (e.g. “first time!”). In Cogita the drawing stands until the card’s “Check”.
live.task: "task" — a different task each time, equally hard: { "require": ["onstep(s, 0.5)", "abs(s - r0) >= 1"], "solve": "w2.pos = 3 + s", "new": "New task", "tries": 200 }
live.task2: values with "random" are drawn (variables and properties of things; a property may be an expression of them: "m": "=a", "pos": "=3 - d") until every "require" condition is true, the task is not solved at the start (no "goal" rule holds) and the "solve" solution can be set by hand (within the limits, on something that may be changed);
live.task3: comparable difficulty comes from the conditions alone: the same steps, numbers from the same range, the result on the slider grid (onstep), far enough from the start. When nothing fits, the task from the "value" values stays. "new" — a “New task” button (false — none); in Cogita every attempt draws the same way and remembers the numbers, and "solve" is the solution of the question unless the question gives its own.
live.panel: "panel" — "below" (controls below the drawing, usual) or "side" (beside it, when the drawing is wide; on a phone always below)
live.elements: In the elements of the drawing:
live.anyNumber: every number (x, y, w, h, r, x2, y2, rotate, scale, opacity, width, size) and colour (fill, stroke) may be an expression: "x": "=x0 + v*t", "fill": "=trafione ? 'ok' : 'accent'"
live.showStep: "show": "step >= 1" — visible only when the condition is true
live.drag: "drag": { "x": "cel" } — dragging sets the value to the finger position (x, y); or { "set": { "kat": "deg(atan2(py, px))" }, "label": "Direction" } — from the finger position (px, py); "label" for screen readers. The handle can be grabbed from 44 px and works with the arrow keys
live.tap: "tap": "run" or { "set": { "widac": "1 - widac" }, "do": "toggle", "go": "next", "label": "Flip" } — a click on the element (also Enter/space)
live.repeat: "repeat": 20 — this many copies of the element; in each "i" (0, 1, …) and "n" (how many) — e.g. gas particles, a scale (up to {n})
live.kinds: new kinds: "arrow" (a vector from x, y to x2, y2; "head" — arrowhead size), "poly" ("points": [[x, y], …] — numbers or "=…"; "closed": true — a polygon),
live.plot: "plot" (a curve: "fn": "A*sin(k*u)" — y of u, or "fx", "fy" — a way; "var" (usually "u"), "from", "to", "samples" (up to {n})),
live.trace: "trace" (a trail: "fx": "x", "fy": "y" — a point every "every" s of simulation, the last "keep" points; cleared on restart),
live.frame: "frame" (a frame with a world: the rectangle x, y, w, h shows a part of the world "view": [x0, y0, x1, y1] — y grows UPWARD, units are e.g. metres; "axes": { "x": "x [m]", "y": "y [m]", "grid": true }, "clip": true — what goes outside the frame disappears;
live.frame2: in a frame positions are in world units and sizes (r, width, size, head) in drawing units; a "rect" stands with its lower-left corner at (x, y); a group in a frame shifts by world x, y and rotates counter-clockwise)
live.world: A world of things ("world") — when the drawing is a set-up of things that are added, moved, hung and removed (a balance of beams and weights, a mobile, gears). You do not write a game, you describe kinds of things, the things at the start and the rules:
live.props: "props": [{ "name": "pos", "value": 1, "min": 0, "max": "=parent.length", "step": 0.25, "unit": "m", "label": "Place", "apart": 0.25, "new": "parent.pivot + 1", "when": "!isroot" }] — properties with limits (limits may be expressions; "apart" — distance from siblings; "new" — where a new thing stands; "when" — when the property applies to the thing),
live.thingLet: "let": [{ "name": "total", "value": "bm + sum(children, total)" }] — values computed in each thing (the order follows from what they read),
live.thingState: "state": [{ "name": "angle", "value": 0, "rate": "omega" }] and "events" — the motion of each thing (the same Runge-Kutta; "sim" then gives only "dt", "speed", "auto", "sleep"),
live.shapes: "shapes": [elements as in "elements"] — the look of one thing, computed in it ("=x" is ITS x; in a frame — world coordinates),
live.thingDrag: "drag": { "pos": "parent.pivot + (px - parent.x)*cos(parent.angle)" } — what dragging sets (the finger in the world: px, py; the handle lies at its "x", "y", radius "hit"),
live.can: "can": { "edit": ["m", "pos"], "add": ["ciezarek"], "remove": true, "copy": true }, "readouts": [{ "label", "value", "unit", "digits" }] (the panel of the chosen thing), "children": 8,
live.brief: "brief": "{m} kg" — what the thing is called in the panel (“Weight 2 kg”); "mark": false — no dashed ring around things that may be changed (when the kind shows it itself: by colour and arrows from "can", "can.pos") }
live.things: "things" — the things at the start: [{ "id": "w1", "kind": "ciezarek", "parent": "b1", "m": 4, "pos": 1.5, "lock": ["m"] }] — properties directly; { "random": [from, to] } — at random (in Cogita on each attempt); "=a + 1" — an expression of the drawing’s values (random tasks); "lock": true — nothing may change, a list — these properties may not
live.allow: "allow" — what is allowed in this world: { "add", "remove", "copy", "edit", "drag" (true/false), "roots": ["belka"] (what may be placed at the top) }; "limits": { "things": 40, "depth": 6 }
live.keep: "keep": [{ "when": "edits <= 2", "say": "Only two moves!" }] — must always hold: a change after which it does not hold is undone; "save": true — a workshop (save, load, JSON); "hint" — a hint when nothing is chosen ({…} — computed)
live.panelGiven: The panel shows what is given (“Given”: things that may not be changed) and what the person sets (“You set”: in a puzzle each changeable property as its own slider, without choosing a thing); "list": true/false forces or turns off these rows (by default: when nothing may be added or removed and there are at most 6).
live.worldEl: In the elements: { "type": "world" } in a frame — the things stand here; frame "camera": true — zooming (+, −, Ctrl+wheel, two fingers) and panning; "view" computed from the things, e.g. "=min(things, bx0)".
live.worldExpr: In the expressions of things: parent.x, root.x, w1.x (a thing by id), outer.x (the one summing up); summaries sum/avg/min/max/count/all/any over a set: children, descendants, siblings, others, things or the name of a kind; built into things: isroot, depth, index, selected, nchildren; in the whole drawing: edits (how many changes since “Start over”), nthings.
live.worldUndo: Every change (drag, panel, adding) goes through the rules of the world and has “Undo” (Ctrl+Z); in Cogita the answer is the arranged world — replayed by the same rules and checked by simulating to the end; solution: "w2.pos = 5". Pattern: the example “Balance — workshop”.
live.builtins: Built-in names: {list} — t: simulation time (s), time: time since the drawing was shown (s; motion without a simulation, e.g. "y": "=sin(2*time)"), step: the place in a presentation scene (0 at its start, 1 after the first step, smoothly in between — for revealing), i/n: copy number and how many copies, u: the course of a curve, px/py: the finger while dragging; edits: how many changes in the world, nthings: how many things; held: 1 while the drawing stands still for a prediction, tries: how many times it was checked; in a thing can: 1 when the person may change it.
live.light: To keep the drawing light (phone): up to about 300 elements, no "blur"/"glow" on many elements, "dt" 0.001–0.005, always "until" or an event with "stop", at most 4–6 controls. The drawing computes only when something changes and stops when it is not visible.
live.physics: Physics — patterns: projectile (x, y, vx, vy; "rate" vy: "-g"), pendulum (th, om; om: "-g/L*sin(th)"), spring (x, v; v: "-k/m*x - c*v"), incline (a = g*(sin − μ·cos)), collision (an event, "set" both velocities at once), refraction (let: angle from asin(n1/n2*sin)), wave ("plot" with "fn" of u and time).

prompt.intro: Prepare the JSON of a drawing to move for the “Animation” module in REcreatio (a page or a presentation; the same drawing can be a question in Cogita).
prompt.topic: Topic: [describe the phenomenon, e.g. “projectile motion — the learner sets the angle and hits the target”].
prompt.rules: Rules: first the person does something (slider, drag, button), then sees the effect; one idea per drawing; labels in English; a goal ("goal") only when it is a task.
prompt.return: Return ONE JSON object with the keys "alt", "size", "elements" and — as needed — "vars", "let", "sim", "controls", "rules", "predict", "task", "panel", "symbols", "world". No comments.

world.givenGroup: Given — you do not change this
world.notLayout: This is not a layout (JSON with a “things” list).

model.predictSay: Predict first: set everything the way you think — then click “Check” and see what happens.

run.nameTaken: this name is already a variable or a computed value
run.notSettable: “{name}” is neither a variable nor simulation state — it cannot be set
run.infinite: the simulation gave infinity or NaN — check “rate” (division by 0?)
run.notAllowed: That is not allowed in this task.

task.unknownKey: “{key}” — there is no such variable or property of a thing (thing.property)
